request: Should we upgrade the web framework to the next major version in this sprint?
facts: The major version we are on stops receiving security fixes in 14 months.
A spike branch on the new version passes 96% of the test suite; every remaining failure is in the session middleware, which one of the two listed breaking changes affects.
In the spike's benchmark, request handling is about 20% faster. Nobody has complained about speed.
The sprint holds one deliverable promised to a customer; doing the upgrade now moves it back by about a week. The customer has said a week's slip is acceptable but that they would rather not have it.
Two of the five engineers have asked for the upgrade for months: three libraries they want to use require the new version.
The upgrade is one pull request; reverting it restores the old version.
note: A trade-off written so that the three default perspectives have reasons to differ: the means works and is reversible, the cost is a slip the customer accepted reluctantly, and the need is the team's rather than a user's. No expected outcome; what is tracked is how often the units land on both sides. In the first run (1.5.1, three runs) every run was rejected 0/3 and graded critical. The units hung on the same facts: the session middleware failures are unfixed and unsized in security-sensitive code (so the one-week estimate and the revert are both doubted), the customer would rather not slip, 14 months of support remain, and the libraries are wanted rather than needed now. The facts lean to reject as written.
